transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-02 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording ID: ff-2026-04-02-nxp-01
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Redwood CSM); Dr. Alan Reyes (CISO), Priya Menon (Head of Compliance), Marc Liu (Platform Engineer), Sophie Carter (Audit Liaison)

Summary: quick posture review for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 readiness. Walkthrough of evidence delivery, trust portal access (we referred to TrustArchive), RBAC/SSO options, KMS integration and audit log exports. Customer requested controls mapping and sample evidence for auditors; we agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- TrustArchive access & permissions model
- SOC 2 Type II report and supporting evidence bundles
- Controls mapping to ISO 27001 Annex A
- RBAC/SSO (SAML, SCIM) and provisioning flow
- Audit log retention, streaming (S3 / Splunk) and residency
- Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM key management and BYOK options

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time today. Uh, quick intro — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Devon our solutions engineer and Laura from CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Dr. Alan Reyes: Good — thanks. Alan here. We, uh, kicked this off because our external auditors want a clearer path for evidence access for our SOC 2 Type II engagement, and also mapping to ISO 27001.
[00:15] Priya Menon: Yep, and we need to confirm log retention and residency before we sign off for production access.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Totally, that's exactly what we wanted to get through. Quick agenda: show how you can access TrustArchive (that's our trust center), what evidence we can deliver, how RBAC and SSO will work for your auditors, and then dive into KMS and log exports. Devon, want to kick off on TrustArchive?
[00:33] Devon Patel: Sure. So TrustArchive is the tenant-specific portal — link is trustarchive.redwood.com/nexapharm (note: placeholder). You get role-based access, and we support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning if you wanna auto-provision auditor accounts. Small caveat — sometimes SCIM attribute mapping needs a one-off tweak for custom LDAP attributes, we've seen that with a couple customers.
[00:50] Marc Liu: When you say role-based access, is that RBAC tied to our IdP groups or separate roles within Redwood?
[00:56] Devon Patel: Good question. It's a mapping: groups from your IdP (SAML/SCIM) map to Redwood roles. So you can have an "auditor" group in your IdP that gets read-only trust-archive access. We also have granular object-level permissions for evidence packages, so you can restrict which service components the auditor sees.
[01:12] Sophie Carter: And will those accesses be logged? We need immutable audit logs for who viewed what and when.
[01:17] Devon Patel: Yes — every TrustArchive access event is logged and can be exported. We stream audit logs to your target (S3, Splunk, or we can push to your SIEM). Note there can be a lag depending on export config, usually near-real-time for syslog, a few minutes for S3 batches.
[01:30] Priya Menon: For retention, we need 3 years of audit trail for certain controls — can you guarantee that?
[01:34] Maya Chen: We persist logs per customer configuration; retention is configurable. If you want 3 years, we can set it and route to your S3 bucket in eu-west-1 and apply lifecycle you control. Devon, add the note about cost implications?
[01:45] Devon Patel: Right — longer retention and higher ingest increases storage costs and egress. We'll include a cost estimate in the controls mapping doc that shows token/event volume assumptions.
[01:55] Dr. Alan Reyes: Okay. About encryption — we run a strict BYOK policy. Do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[02:01] Devon Patel: Yes. Redwood supports KMS integration via your cloud provider KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we also support external HSM/BYOK flows. There are two patterns: platform-managed keys and customer-managed keys. With CMKs, you control rotation and key policies. A note though — for some private deployment nodes we have an extra step to sync key access, but it's standard. Sometimes the terminology in our docs gets transcribed as "K M S sync" or similar.
[02:19] Priya Menon: Are there any caveats for private deployments and SOC evidence? Auditors will want a chain of custody.
[02:24] Maya Chen: For Private deployments (VPC or on-prem), we provide a dedicated evidence bundle plus an auditor read-only account in TrustArchive. If it's on-prem air-gapped, we do a packaged evidence export you can hand to auditors.
[02:36] Marc Liu: For the control mapping, we need a CSV that maps our control IDs to your control evidence artifacts. Do you have a template?
[02:42] Devon Patel: We do. We'll send a mapping CSV with columns: our_control_id, your_control_id, control_description, artifact_link, evidence_type, sample_log_path. We'll also include a sample mapping to ISO Annex A clauses for the most common controls.
[02:55] Sophie Carter: Will you include sample artifacts? like screen captures or logs?
[02:59] Devon Patel: Yes, the evidence bundle includes redactable screenshots, configuration export, config-as-code snippets, and log samples. We sometimes sanitize PII in log samples before bundling.
[03:08] Dr. Alan Reyes: About certifications: do you provide the SOC 2 Type II report itself and any bridge letters?
[03:12] Maya Chen: We can share the SOC 2 Type II report and this quarter's bridge notes if applicable. For ISO 27001, we provide a statement of applicability and supporting docs where available — note that full ISO certificates are typically tied to the entity that performed the audit but we do provide the artifacts we control.
[03:27] Priya Menon: On SSO — our auditors want time-limited auditor sessions and just-in-time access. Can SCIM do ephemeral accounts?
[03:33] Devon Patel: SCIM provisioning can create accounts; you can combine it with short-lived roles or configure your IdP for just-in-time provisioning and limited session durations. We also support expiring links from TrustArchive for temporary read-only access.
[03:45] Maya Chen: Quick sidebar — several customers set up an "auditor" org-level group and we only provision auditors into that group during the audit window.
[03:50] Marc Liu: One more — log format. We ingest JSON logs; will you accept structured logs or do you transform them?
[03:56] Devon Patel: We accept structured JSON and syslog. If your logs are structured, we preserve fields; if not, we apply a normalization layer. For exports to third-party SIEMs we keep original payload and add our event metadata.
[04:10] Priya Menon: Data residency: we need all PII and patient-related tokens to remain in EU.
[04:15] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll pin your tenant to eu-west-1 and ensure data-at-rest is in that region. Note: backups and cold storage locations are controlled by the region config, we'll include that in the mapping doc.
[04:24] Sophie Carter: Auditors may ask for chain-of-custody for model weights and artifacts — do you log model uploads and versions?
[04:30] Devon Patel: Yes, model versioning events, upload metadata, and who triggered deploys are logged. We keep a deployment history you can export as CSV for audit evidence.
[04:38] Dr. Alan Reyes: Excellent. On the controls matrix, can you show a sample mapping for encryption controls to ISO A.8/A.10?
[04:44] Devon Patel: We'll include that in the CSV. Example row we discussed: Redwood-KMS-01 -> Nexa-ENC-03 -> "Data encryption at rest" -> artifact link (KMS policy export) -> evidence_type: policy + key rotation logs.
[04:56] Maya Chen: Ok, let's capture action owners: I'll send the SOC 2 report and TrustArchive link. Devon will create the controls mapping CSV and ISO sample mapping. Marc and Sophie to confirm log targets and auditor contact.
[05:07] Marc Liu: Will you allow us to test a log stream before the retention policy is finalized? We'd like to send a week of logs to test parsing.
[05:12] Devon Patel: Yep, we can set up a temporary ingestion for a test bucket with short retention. That will help us show parsing examples to your auditors too.
[05:20] Priya Menon: Any third-party subprocessor list we can share with auditors?
[05:24] Maya Chen: Yes, we maintain a subprocessors list in TrustArchive and we can export a PDF copy of our current subprocessors and their locations.
[05:31] Dr. Alan Reyes: On the topic of remediation evidence — if a control fails in your environment for a day, do you provide a post-mortem artifact that auditors accept?
[05:38] Devon Patel: We provide incident timelines, root cause analysis, and remediation notes. Those go into the evidence bundle; sometimes auditors want additional corroborating logs which we also include if available.
[05:46] Sophie Carter: For the private deployment demo, who should join from Redwood? We need someone who can talk about network isolation and key management.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Devon can lead that; we also recommend an infra engineer present, we'll coordinate availability.
[05:58] Dr. Alan Reyes: Good. A couple of clarifying points: will the evidence bundle include raw logs or redacted samples?
[06:03] Devon Patel: We provide both where possible: a redacted sample for the auditor and optionally raw logs delivered to your S3 bucket if you authorize it.
[06:11] Priya Menon: Do you have a support SLA for auditors accessing TrustArchive during an audit weekend?
[06:15] Laura Kim: We offer a "white glove" audit support add-on that guarantees a named support contact and accelerated response for audit windows. I'll send the package details after this call.
[06:23] Marc Liu: On the controls CSV, will you indicate which artifacts are single-file downloads vs. APIs?
[06:28] Devon Patel: Yes we will. We'll mark artifact delivery method and include direct links and API endpoints for programmatic pulls.
[06:34] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap and confirm dates. Next steps: Maya shares SOC 2 and TrustArchive link by 2026-04-06; Devon produces controls CSV and ISO sample mapping by 2026-04-09; Marc confirms log target by 2026-04-07; Sophie provides auditor contact by 2026-04-10; schedule private-deploy demo w/c 2026-04-12.
[06:52] Dr. Alan Reyes: That sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood's side?
[06:56] Devon Patel: No blockers. There might be minor SCIM mapping tweaks but nothing that would delay audit access.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the demo and attach the evidence links. Thanks everyone.
[07:07] Priya Menon: Thanks.
[07:08] (call ends)
